newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up after SBI sells dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up after SBI sells dollars.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended up against the dollar at 35.785/790 on Wednesday after the State Bank of India (SBI) resorted to heavy dollar selling, dealers said.
"The market was long on dollars," said a dealer.
"SBI sold heavily, taking the rupee below the 35.80-mark," she said. The rupee saw a high of 35.78/79 on Wednesday.
"SBI dumped dollars today," another dealer commented.
SBI is a major force in the foreign exchange market but it is usually a dollar buyer, dealers said.
The rupee gave way as there was no central bank intervention to defend the dollar, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India has been buying dollars in recent weaks to stop the rupee from piercing the 35.81/82 barrier.
The forward dollar market was uneventful on Wednesday.
"The forward market hardly moved today," said a dealer.
The six month annualised premium closed at 3.40 percent, up from the previous close of 3.30 percent, dealers said.
